root_cause.text: In the XFS subsystem, `xfs_unmount_flush_inodes()` incorrectly flushes the Active Item List (AIL) while background reclaim and inode garbage collection (inodegc) are still running, allowing inodegc to dirty and insert inodes into the AIL and background reclaim to race to free dirty inodes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows `xfs_ail_push_all_sync(mp->m_ail)` being moved to execute after `xfs_inodegc_stop(mp)` and `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&mp->m_reclaim_work)`, and the commit message explains that "background reclaim and inodegc should not be running while the AIL is being pushed during unmount, as inodegc can dirty and insert inodes into the AIL during the flush, and background reclaim can race to abort and free dirty inodes."

intent_record.intent_summary: Delay the synchronous AIL push until after background inode garbage collection and reclaim work are stopped to prevent metadata updates during unmount.
intent_record.what: The function call to xfs_ail_push_all_sync is relocated from before xfs_inodegc_stop and cancel_delayed_work_sync to immediately after them.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that background inode garbage collection and pending reclaim work are completely stopped before the Active Items List (AIL) is synchronously flushed, preventing background processes from dirtying more metadata during unmount.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the `xfs_unmount_flush_inodes()` function, which contains the vulnerable sequence of operations. Specifically, on line 664, it flushes the AIL using `xfs_ail_push_all_sync(mp->m_ail)` before cancelling the background reclaim work on line 665 (`cancel_delayed_work_sync(&mp->m_reclaim_work)`). Furthermore, there is no mechanism to stop or flush the inode garbage collection (inodegc) before pushing the AIL, allowing both background reclaim and inodegc to run concurrently and race during the AIL flush.
